title: Assawanama
summary: A Fresh Pond place name at Fort Salonga, connected with Huntington-Smithtown boundary history and several related recorded forms.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Fresh Pond point in Fort Salonga; not a surveyed historical boundary.
why_this_matters: Assawanama preserves a Fresh Pond placename at Fort Salonga, where the name includes several related, disputed, or overlapping forms. Interpretive context connects the name with fishing-place meanings, while the variant spellings show how complex Native geography could become tangled in colonial documentation. Careful history sometimes means holding uncertainty while still recognizing water, fish, and local knowledge as central to Indigenous Long Island.
introduction_content: Assawanama names Fresh Pond in Huntington town, at the boundary area between Huntington and Smithtown. The same pond is also associated with earlier recorded forms including Unchemau, Unshemamuck, and Oshamamucks.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Assawanama, Unchemau, Unshemamuck, Oshamamucks, Fresh Pond, and the disputed Cowamoke/Cowamok form. Assawanama is interpreted as a mid-way fishing place, while Unshemamuck/Oshamamucks is interpreted as an eel fishing-place. Cowamoke is explained as a pine-tree place but treated as a likely mistaken attribution for Fresh Pond.

Additional recorded forms include UntHemamuck, Unsheamuk, Unchemau, Unshemamuke, and Oshamamucks.

Why Place Names Matter

“The names that people give to places can be clues to the history of the name-givers or aspects of national and world history.”

— Xolile P. Ntshangase, Renaming as representation of community onomastic interests: A case study of Alfred Duma Municipality (2025), introduction
whereintheworld_content: Approximate general point near modern Fresh Pond at Fort Salonga, on the Huntington-Smithtown boundary landscape. The map placement is for orientation, not an exact deed-boundary coordinate.
